basis: Assumption: the lap's compound is two or more C-numbers harder than the race's MEDIUM (only at races whose labels skip a C-number, e.g. C1/C3/C4). Extends the one-step HARD value by a smaller step, because a hard tyre still slides when following. A per-lap sensitivity, NOT tyre wear. Source: WC-16 research, _evidence/WC-16-2026-10-31/c_numbers_report.md (option B)

Assumption: one C-number harder than the race's MEDIUM. Same value as the WC-13 relative HARD factor, so a consecutive C3-medium race keeps the WC-13 values; 0.96 not 0.95 for the WC-13 archived-method reason (BUILD-ORDER rule 6). Source: _evidence/WC-16-2026-10-31/c_numbers_report.md
Reference (1.00): the race's MEDIUM compound; the race value is read as the cost on the middle compound. Source: _evidence/WC-16-2026-10-31/c_numbers_report.md

Assumption: one C-number softer than the race's MEDIUM. Same value as the WC-13 relative SOFT factor: a car in the wake slides more and runs hotter tyre surfaces, and a softer compound overheats sooner. NOT tyre wear. Source: _evidence/WC-16-2026-10-31/c_numbers_report.md

Assumption: two or more C-numbers softer than the race's MEDIUM (only at skip races, e.g. 2022 Australia C2/C3/C5). Extends the one-step SOFT value by a smaller second step. Source: _evidence/WC-16-2026-10-31/c_numbers_report.md

Neutral (1.00): the race's MEDIUM is C2. The research proposed 0.97 (shift by how soft the race's medium is); dropped by owner ruling DD-WC29 (2026-10-31) because the shift put 23 per-lap values on archived-method numbers at 3 dp and no small nudge cleared them; rule 6 stays strict. Row kept at 1.00 so a calibrated shift can slot in later. Source: _evidence/WC-16-2026-10-31/c_numbers_report.md
